title.en: A patient asks about copper peptides

lead.en: She has seen a GHK-Cu serum online and asks whether to start it.

label.en: GHK-Cu serum is the standard first step.

label.en: Offer the injection instead. It is the stronger form.

why.en: Injected GHK-Cu is a different product: no randomized trials, injection-site pain and rash are common because copper irritates tissue, and in the US the injectable route sits outside the Category 1 listing.

title.en: Injected GHK-Cu is a different product

rationale.en: There are no randomized trials of injection, injection-site pain and rash are common because copper irritates tissue, and in the United States the injectable route sits outside the Category 1 listing that covers non-injectable use.

practice.en: Whatever your role, name the route every time you talk about this peptide.
Do not prescribe GHK-Cu for injection.
If a patient tells you they inject GHK-Cu, record the product, where it was bought and any site reactions, and bring it to the prescriber. Do not advise on amounts or technique.
Anyone injecting a copper peptide should be pointed to a prescriber, not to a better supplier.
